providers.title: Uniform component bound
providers.scope: Every real step bound D: all connected components of the graph joining Gaussian primes at distance at most D have at most B_D vertices; no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes has steps at most D.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Residues modulo a split prime
providers.scope: Gaussian primes of norm p = 1 mod 4: the residue field has p elements and is represented by integers; nonzero multiples have length at least sqrt(p); divisibility by both conjugate factors means divisibility by p.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Periodic reduction
providers.scope: D >= 1 and a finite set P of primes 1 mod 4 whose sieve set A(P) contains no infinite D-walk: every component of the Gaussian-prime graph has at most |E| + (K_D - 1)|E|Q^2 vertices, Q the product of P.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Size of a batch
providers.scope: Primes 1 mod 4 in [T, 2T]: their number is (1/2 + o(1)) T/log T, and k_T log(2T) <= (8 log 2) T for T >= 2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Pinsker's inequality
providers.scope: Probability laws on a finite set: relative entropy (natural logarithms) is at least twice the squared total variation distance.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Continuity of conditional entropy
providers.scope: Pairs of finite variables on a product set of at most a elements with total variation at most e <= 1/2: conditional entropies differ by at most 2h(e) + 2e log a.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Short lists
providers.scope: Finite variables X (at most a values) and Y, lists L(y): log a - H(X|Y) >= rho log(a/b) - h(rho), where rho is the probability that X is on a list of size at most b.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Concavity over random coordinates
providers.scope: Exchangeable random index sequences independent of a finite variable Y: the average joint entropy of the first s coordinates is concave in s.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: One shared conditioning cost
providers.scope: Index sequences with uniform marginals: high average joint entropy and a cheap shared conditioning variable give small average conditional deficit per coordinate, with no independence assumption.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hoeffding's inequality
providers.scope: Independent real variables with values in [a_j, b_j]: P(S - ES >= t) <= exp(-2t^2 / sum (b_j - a_j)^2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Binomial lower tail
providers.scope: Binomial law with n trials and success probability lambda, 0 < v < 1: P(B <= (1-v) n lambda) <= exp(-n lambda v^2 / 2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Edge isoperimetry of the cube
providers.scope: Nonempty sets S of vertices of {0,1}^r: at least |S| log2(2^r/|S|) edges leave S.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Many differences
providers.scope: Stretches of n steps of a D-walk, A = diameter times width: (pi/24) n <= A <= D^2 n^2 and at least A/(pi D^2) distinct differences; the proof uses Brouwer's fixed-point theorem.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Signed products avoid thin rectangles
providers.scope: Distinct primes 1 mod 4 in [T, 2T], T >= 5, 0 < d < 1/4, d^3 r >= 2, centred rectangles with R W <= P^(1-d): a random product of conjugate factors has a nonzero multiple in the rectangle with probability at most exp(-d^3 r/(640 log 2)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Entropy enrichment
providers.scope: Any D-walk, a batch of primes in [T, 2T], g^5 U >= K_D log T, q <= k: sampling an endpoint of a uniformly random distinct difference of the next exp(gU) steps halves the residue entropy deficit up to 16g.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Coverage transfer
providers.scope: Finite abelian residue groups of orders in [T, 2T] on a lattice: coverage of all continuation laws at a later checkpoint, nearly maximal joint entropy and a cheap shared vector of continuations give coverage with a larger exponent at the earlier checkpoint.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Terminal coverage
providers.scope: The common sampling schedule, any D-walk, large M: from every exact start at every checkpoint, the final residues have coverage for all but a small fraction of the signed coordinates of each batch.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Information cost of a batch
providers.scope: D-walks avoiding both zero classes of every sieving prime: each batch near T forces at least c_1/log T units of conditional information per increment at the common final time.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite sieve obstruction
providers.scope: Every D >= 1: a finite set of primes 1 mod 4 whose sieve set contains no infinite D-walk.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
